summary: For our ancestors, observing the stars was not merely an act of contemplation; it was a precise science that guided the management of water resources and the administration of justice. Today, the 'SPHEREx' mission utilizes the latest data from NASA to demonstrate that the Omanis were pioneers in interpreting the movements of the cosmos. In other words, the celestial expanse captured by SPHEREx today is the very same sky that the Omanis observed in ancient times. What our ancestors discerned through the naked eye and empirical experience, SPHEREx data now confirms with absolute scientific precision.

Report: Planet X Challenge and the SPHEREx Mission

Proposed Solution: “Star Guide” — A Website for Tracking Two Stars

1. Challenge Overview

NASA’s SPHEREx mission surveys the sky and creates a map of the entire sky by collecting data in 102

bands of near-infrared light. The challenge is to create a public-facing web tool that presents SPHEREx

images and data in an interactive and accessible way, helping users explore astronomical observations over

time.

2. Proposed Solution: “Star Guide” Website

The project proposes an interactive website focused on Al-Dabaran and Al-Thurayya. It will present

information about these two celestial references and explain their connection to the traditional organization

of falaj water distribution in Al-Thabiti village. The website will combine the inherited local account with

modern astronomical information and SPHEREx resources.

3. How the Website Works

• Explore the two stars: Learn about Al-Dabaran and Al-Thurayya and view their astronomical information.

• Explore the sky over time: Use available astronomical data to view the stars for selected dates and times.

• Discover the heritage: Read how ancestors in Al-Thabiti village used these stars when organizing falaj water

turns.

• Understand the connection: See how the project brings traditional water-allocation knowledge together with

modern astronomical observations.

4. The Omani Element: Al-Thabiti Falaj and Traditional Star-Based Water Allocation

The idea for this project came from the traditional knowledge of our ancestors in Al-Thabiti village. According

to the local heritage that inspired the project, our ancestors used the stars Al-Dabaran and Al-Thurayya

when organizing and dividing the water turns of Falaj Al-Thabiti among farm owners. This practice reflects

the careful observation of the sky and the engineering knowledge used by earlier generations to manage a

shared water resource. The project uses SPHEREx as a modern astronomical resource to revisit this

knowledge and highlight the connection between observations of the stars and the traditional system. The

website will document this local story and explain how falaj water distribution supported farms and the

community.

5. Suggested Data Sources

The resources listed in the challenge description include the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive and

SPHEREx resources; SPHEREx tutorial notebooks that demonstrate how to work with the data using

Python; Gaia Mission Data Release 3 (DR3), which can support the exploration of star positions and

properties; and WiseView as an example of a public tool for exploring data from the earlier WISE mission.

The two stars highlighted by the project are Al-Dabaran and Al-Thurayya.

6. Key Points to Highlight

• Core challenge: Turn SPHEREx astronomical data into an interactive, accessible web experience for the public.

• Core solution: Explore Al-Dabaran and Al-Thurayya and document their traditional role in organizing Falaj Al

Thabiti water turns.

• Omani identity: Preserve the heritage of Al-Thabiti village and the ancestors’ star-based method of dividing falaj

water among farm owners.

• Development resources: SPHEREx, NASA/IPAC, Python tutorial notebooks, Gaia DR3, and WiseView as an

inspiration.
